## ✨ Highlights

New kernels on both tracks, a smaller kernel attack surface, and Consul
services named after their cluster.

- 🐧 **Linux 7.3.3** on the stable track (from 7.2.15) and **6.18.62**
  on the longterm track (from 6.18.60) - the longterm one with a
  critical netfilter fix.
- ✂️ **No io_uring**: nothing on a node uses it, and it is one of the
  kernel's busiest sources of vulnerabilities - about 35 fewer of this
  year's kernel CVEs apply to Janus's build.
- 🏷️ **Consul: a node's HAProxy services are named after its cluster**
  (`haproxy-<cluster>-<frontend>`), and its token may register its own
  cluster's only.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Consul consumers selecting Janus services by name** - `haproxy-url`,
  `haproxy-<frontend>`, `haproxy-exporter` - see them renamed
  `haproxy-<cluster>-url` and so on (`haproxy-<node>-...` for a node
  alone) as each node updates: select them by their tags instead
  (`haproxy`, `url`), which finds the old names and the new alike
  ([the guide](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/consul-controller.md#prometheus-the-exporters-and-the-urls)).
  Update the Controller first: until a node is updated, its token keeps
  the older right and its services stay registered; the Controller's
  next Consul pass after the node's update takes that right off.
- **An update whose kernel couldn't drive the machine is refused**
  before anything is switched - its boot disk, its network interfaces.
  Today's kernels drive every machine Janus supports, so nothing is
  refused yet; `-allow-unsupported-hardware` (janusctl `lifecycle
  upgrade`/`install`) is for a machine whose devices change before it
  boots the release.

## 🔄 Since the v2026.11.08-2 pre-release

What its lab campaign found ([#595](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/595)), fixed in [#596](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/596):

- **A node updated after the Controller loses the older Consul right**:
  the Controller gave its layer, scope included, to the nodes still on
  the release before, which drop the field and keep the rest. Updated,
  such a node kept that layer, and the Controller, seeing the same
  layer, never gave it again - the node's token kept the right to any
  `haproxy-…` service. A node now says what its HAProxy services are
  named after (`ConsulManagedGetResponse.scope`): the Controller takes
  the older right off as soon as the node names them after its scope,
  and gives the layer again, once, to a node whose layer lacks it.
- **`janusctl network consul managed` prints the scope** the node's
  HAProxy services are named after, and the Controller's **Consul**
  tab shows each node's (`writes haproxy-<scope>-…`) and a node still
  on the older right.

## 🔒 Security

- **Linux kernel (longterm) 6.18.60 → 6.18.62** - nodes on the longterm
  kernel track (a schematic with `"kernel": "longterm"`); the stable
  track's nodes aren't concerned:
  - 🔴 critical [CVE-2026-80668](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-80668) - netfilter: nf_conntrack_expect: use conntrack GC to reap expectations
  - ⚫ unknown [CVE-2026-99076](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99076) - ipv6: udp: Create exceptions before socket matching
  - ⚫ unknown [CVE-2026-99283](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99283) - netfilter: conntrack: tcp: use UNACK timeout for non-closing RST packets
  - ⚫ unknown [CVE-2026-99284](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-99284) - net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()
  - 18 more don't apply to Janus's build.

## 🐧 Kernel

- **Stable track: Linux 7.3.3** (7.2.15 before). 7.3 folds
  `PROC_SYSCTL` into `SYSCTL`.
- **Longterm track: Linux 6.18.62** (6.18.60 before).
- **io_uring off on both tracks**: `IO_URING`, `IO_URING_ZCRX` and
  `IO_WQ` gone - HAProxy, the Go daemons, keepalived, BIRD and the
  guest agent don't use it.

## 🧰 Nodes

- **An update checks the target kernel can drive the machine**: the
  release's image says which drivers its kernel has, and `Upgrade` and
  `Install` compare them with what the boot disk and the network
  interfaces are bound to; a refused release is never switched to, and
  `Rollback` won't switch to it either. janusd logs, once a boot, what
  the devices are bound to.
- **Consul**: HAProxy services named after the node's cluster, or the
  node alone; `ConsulManaged.scope` says which
  ([consul](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/consul.md#from-the-controller)).

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Consul tokens by scope**: each node's token writes its own scope's
  HAProxy services only (`janus-scope-<scope>`); `janus-nodes` no longer
  lets a node write any `haproxy-...`. A node of an older release keeps
  that right until it updates.

## 🔌 The node API

- `ConsulManaged.scope` (new): what the node's HAProxy services are
  named after, the Controller's word; `ConsulManagedGetResponse.scope`
  (new): what the node names them after now.
- `ImageSource.allow_unsupported_hardware` (new): install or update a
  release whose kernel doesn't drive the machine's devices as they are.
